title: nth-child formulas
summary: :nth-child(3n), (n + 4), (-n + 3) and :nth-last-child pick items by position with a formula.
explanation: :nth-child(An + B) matches the items whose position fits the formula for n = 0, 1, 2… Positions start at 1. 3n is every third item (3, 6, 9), n + 4 is the fourth onwards, and -n + 3 is the first three only.
:nth-last-child counts from the end, so :nth-last-child(-n + 2) is the last two. The grid has twelve tiles and each rule paints one pattern; change the formulas and watch which tiles light up.
nth-child counts every sibling, whatever its type or class. If you mix element types and only want to count paragraphs, :nth-of-type counts just siblings of the same tag.

Look at tile 12: the last rule makes it white, but its text stays orange. .tile:nth-child(n + 4):nth-child(even) has two pseudo-classes, so it is more specific than .tile:nth-last-child(-n + 2), and for color the more specific rule wins wherever it comes in the file.
tryThis: Change 3n to 2n + 1: the odd tiles get the border.
Change n + 4 to n + 7: only tiles 8, 10 and 12 keep the orange text.
Change -n + 3 in the first rule to 4n + 1: the first tile of each row turns orange.
